knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 2,\ 0\le v\le 2\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 4 v^{2},\,- u^{2} + v,\,u^{2}\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 0,\,- 2 u,\,2 u\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 8 v,\,1,\,0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 0 & - 2 u & 2 u \\ 8 v & 1 & 0\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - 2 u,\,16 u v,\,16 u v\rangle
$$

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(- 2 u\right)^2+\left(16 u v\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(16 u v\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{512 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 u^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{4 u^{2} \left(128 v^{2} + 1\right)} \\ &=2 u \sqrt{128 v^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

On $D$, both parameters are nonnegative, so $\sqrt{u^2}=|u|=u$.

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D 2 u \sqrt{128 v^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $2 u \sqrt{128 v^{2} + 1}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.

knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 2,\ 0\le v\le 1\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle v,\,u,\,u^{2} - 2 v^{2}\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 0,\,1,\,2 u\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 1,\,0,\,- 4 v\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 u \\ 1 & 0 & - 4 v\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - 4 v,\,2 u,\,-1\rangle
$$

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(- 4 v\right)^2+\left(2 u\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(-1\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{4 u^{2} + 16 v^{2} + 1} \\ &=\sqrt{4 u^{2} + 16 v^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \sqrt{4 u^{2} + 16 v^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $\sqrt{4 u^{2} + 16 v^{2} + 1}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.

knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 2,\ 0\le v\le 1\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u,\,v,\,- 5 u + 2 v\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,\,0,\,-5\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,\,1,\,2\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle 5,\,-2,\,1\rangle
$$

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(5\right)^2+\left(-2\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(1\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{30} \\ &=\sqrt{30}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \sqrt{30}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $\sqrt{30}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.
